concepts.label: Field Level Encryption (FLE)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - fresh sdk:-scoped concept. This page describes client-side per-field encryption performed by the SDK before a document reaches the server ('This is a client-side implementation, with encryption and decryption handled by the Couchbase client SDK'). Deliberately NOT reusing encryption:native-encryption-at-rest, encryption:data-encryption-key or encryption:master-password - those describe Couchbase Server encrypting whole documents/files on disk with server-managed keys, a completely different mechanism from this page's field-level, client-managed, pre-transmission encryption. No page anywhere states a relationship between the two, so no relation is asserted between them either.

cross_component_finding: This page (titled 'Field Level Encryption' in its H1 and frontmatter) is the encryption/certificate judgment call flagged for this round: it is unambiguously client-side SDK field encryption, not Couchbase Server's server-side encryption-at-rest. The page states this directly - 'This is a client-side implementation, with encryption and decryption handled by the Couchbase client SDK' - and never once mentions disk encryption, the Data Encryption Key, the master password, or any node-level key material. The registry's promoted encryption:native-encryption-at-rest / encryption:data-encryption-key / encryption:master-password / encryption:key-rotation concepts all describe Couchbase Server encrypting bytes on disk with server-managed keys; none of that machinery appears here. I therefore minted a fresh sdk:field-level-encryption concept rather than reusing any encryption:* id, per the round's explicit instruction not to reuse the server-side ids just because both mechanisms use the word 'encryption'.
